correctness.rationale: For all positive block compositions, telescoping the floor-coding gives cumulative block weights as a fixed integer vector plus monotone indicators at distinct rotation thresholds. Invertibility of cumulative weights proves distinct orbit classes; irrational density and rational q-grid exact counting give their frequencies. The selected positive-length boundaries of an irrational rotation can approach arbitrary ordered targets, implying the simplex density and entropy endpoint statements. Boundary cases r=1 and rational repeated residues are included. Two standalone checking scripts passed 93,552 and 8,370 cases. No finite search substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The new exact group quotient is asserted for every contiguous-block Young product, for rational as well as irrational mechanical words, with every quotient-class frequency and the full irrational frequency-simplex density law. Launer–Puzynina–Voloshinova (2026), Section 3, establishes existence of each intermediate group complexity by suffix-permutation groups, but neither all Young subgroups nor orbit-frequency distributions. Section 6 treats periodic complexity stability, not the residue formula. Abelian-square-rich words (2017), Section 5, supplies the individual-block rotation interval criterion, credited as a component; its quoted claims do not state the joint Young quotient or entropy flexibility. Research-index semantic queries and dedicated literature queries did not return this full claim. An unstated derivation from classical interval tools or unindexed equivalent remains a nonzero priority risk.
residual_risks: These statements combine well-known rotation interval tools; an existing general proposition could already subsume the new group-orbit frequency law without using this terminology.
The 2004 article was inspected from an abstract/preview rather than every section; complete comparison might reveal a closer formulation.

value.rationale: The 2026 group-complexity literature asks which orbit counts are realized by position-permutation subgroups. For every consecutive-block Young subgroup this result gives a complete classification and exact class measures, with a sharp irrational-rational arithmetic split. The fixed r+1 orbit count despite dense variation of all r+1 class frequency vectors and arbitrarily near-extreme Shannon entropy establishes a structural contrast between orbit count and the distribution of orbit mass; it is not a finite table, arbitrary slice, or mere renaming of an invariant.
